canonical_name: Markov property of solutions of stochastic differential equations
canonical_statement: For a time-homogeneous Ito SDE dX_t = b(X_t) dt + sigma(X_t) dW_t whose hypotheses give a unique solution from every initial state, the resulting solution family is Markov with respect to its filtration, with transition law determined only by the current state and elapsed time.
domains_and_universes: Provisional finite-dimensional state and Brownian noise spaces over Real, a filtered probability space, measurable coefficient functions b and sigma, and a family of solutions indexed by initial states; exact dimensions and Lean universes remain open.
ordered_binders: filtered probability space and Brownian motion W
solution family X started from each initial state
times 0 <= s <= t and bounded measurable test function f
hypotheses: a solution exists from every admitted initial state
the uniqueness notion needed by the selected theorem is satisfied
adaptedness, measurability, integrability, and filtration conditions needed by the stochastic integrals hold
conclusion: A conditional-expectation or transition-kernel Markov identity: the conditional law of the future given the present filtration depends on the past only through the current state.
degenerate_cases: Zero noise, deterministic dynamics, nonunique solutions, explosive solutions, random initial data, completed/right-continuous filtrations, and s = t must be tested explicitly; nonuniqueness cannot be hidden by selecting an arbitrary solution.
alternate_encodings: conditional expectation identity for bounded measurable test functions
conditional distribution identity through a transition kernel
semigroup identity for deterministic initial states
strong Markov identity at stopping times (strictly stronger branch unless derived)
